q1_heap_and_drum.query: Context: we run an open-source, 3D-printed (PLA) auger powder doser for self-driving labs in alloy discovery for additive manufacturing. A 25 mm OD tube with a 21 mm bore and a helical flight ends in a 3 mm outlet; a NEMA 11 stepper turns it at 1-109 rpm, servos tilt it 0-90 degrees, a solenoid taps it, and doses fall onto a 0.1 mg analytical balance. We record a dosing fingerprint (mass per revolution vs tilt and speed, mass per tap, afterflow, no-flow fraction) on 13 powders (NaCl, gas-atomized AlSi10Mg, silicon, rice flours, xanthan gum, carboxymethyl cellulose, BaCl2 dihydrate, fumed silica and others) and calibrate a LIGGGHTS DEM twin. Property labels from handbooks limit our models (angle-of-repose ranges 6-16 degrees wide), so we are designing ten small in-house tests built around the doser, each using a few grams and run on the same jar and day as the fingerprint: (1) heap angle of repose on a 20 mm fixed pedestal on the balance, photographed in silhouette; (2) bulk and tapped density in a 10 mL Class A cylinder filled by the auger and tapped by a cam drop of 3 mm at 250 taps/min, column height read by camera; (3) a servo tilting plate with an IMU: wall friction of a 25 mm powder-filled ring at 70-450 Pa on PLA, stainless steel and glass, and the start angle of 1-5 mm powder layers; (4) particle size and shape from backlit images with a Raspberry Pi HQ camera and a 0.12-1.8x zoom lens; (5) a 25 mm cup with 1-6 mm orifice discs and a servo gate emptying onto the balance (Beverloo fit, smallest orifice that flows, with and without taps); (6) humidity chambers held by saturated salt solutions (MgCl2, Mg(NO3)2, NaCl, KCl, silica gel) with SHT45 sensors, weighing uptake and dosing before and after; (7) a 40 mm by 15 mm rotating drum driven by the doser's stepper, 1-20 rpm; (8) unconfined yield strength of a 20 mm by 40 mm column from a split mould after 0.2-2 kPa consolidation, crushed by a lead-screw platen on a 100 g load cell; (9) a blade spreading a 0.1-0.2 mm layer over a 100 x 30 mm coupon at 10-100 mm/s; (10) a Faraday cup (aluminium cup in a grounded can) with a femtoamp op-amp charge amplifier under the doser outlet. For tests (1) and (7): what does the literature report on (a) fixed-base (pedestal) angle-of-repose tests compared with ISO 4324 funnel pouring, the lifting cylinder and the tilting box: the effect of base diameter relative to particle size (how many particle diameters before the angle stops depending on base size), pour height and rate, feeding from a screw instead of a funnel, image analysis of heap profiles versus the apex formula, repeatability (standard deviation over repeat pours) and inter-method differences; (b) small rotating drums (GranuDrum 84 mm, Revolution Powder Analyzer, and drums under 50 mm): the effect of drum diameter, depth and end-wall friction on the dynamic angle and avalanche statistics, the Froude-number regimes, the cohesive index definitions, and how many particle diameters a drum must span; (c) DEM studies that simulated these exact tests for calibration and how well the calibrated parameters transferred to other flows. Give numbers for table salt, gas-atomized metal AM powders (AlSi10Mg, 316L, Ti-6Al-4V) and fine cohesive powders.
